issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) on SealSaloon (see UML and commented Main usage), but the solution implements a static method named receiveDelivery(String, int, int) instead. This name mismatch between the specification/template and the solution is a structural inconsistency that can confuse students about the required API and cause tests or example code to reference a method that does not exist in the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution's receiveDelivery method to acceptSupplyDelivery (keeping the same parameters and static modifier), or alternatively update the problem statement and template references to use receiveDelivery. Ensure the method name used in UML, template Main, and the solution is identical so students and tests target the same API.

issues.description: The problem specification repeatedly names the static delivery method acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) (UML and description), but the solution implementation uses a differently named static method receiveDelivery(String, int, int). This is a direct identifier mismatch for the same conceptual operation (accepting a supply delivery), which will confuse students mapping requirements to the reference implementation or tests that expect the name from the problem statement.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent name for the static delivery method. Rename the solution's receiveDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) to acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) (or add an acceptSupplyDelivery wrapper that calls receiveDelivery) so the implementation matches the method name used in the problem statement and UML.
